newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Bolger says won't enter bidding war after NZ poll.
newsitem.headline: Bolger says won't enter bidding war after NZ poll.

text.p: Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Sunday he would not enter a "bidding war" as New Zealand faced tough coalition-building negotiations after an inconclusive general election.

"I don't see a bidding war at all. I have no intention of getting into a bidding war. My only interest is good government," Bolger told reporters in his home constituency of Te Kuiti in the North Island.
"We will speak to all the parties over the next 24 to 48 hours. That is an obligation on us," he said.

Bolger said he would not be surprised if New Zealand First leader Winston Peters, who holds the balance of power between Bolger's conservative National Party and Labour, wanted to talk to both simultaneously.
"I would imagine Mr Peters and his advisers will want to carefully assess the options they have," he said.
